body:
A package that has not arrived when you expected it is stressful, especially when you are running low on a product you use every day. In most cases a delay has an ordinary explanation, and there is a clear sequence of checks that finds it. This guide walks through that sequence in the order that saves the most time: work out whether the parcel is actually late, read the tracking correctly, look for a delivery notice, confirm the address, contact the carrier and then contact us. It also explains what happens if a parcel is returned, lost, stolen or damaged, based on our published [shipping policy](/shipping/). It is written for adults aged 21 and over.

## 1. Check the timeline honestly
Delivery has two parts. First comes processing: 24 to 72 business hours after your payment is confirmed, during which we prepare and ship the order. Second comes carrier transit: our published estimates are about 3 to 7 business days for the West Coast (Arizona, Nevada, Washington and Idaho) and about 11 to 18 business days for the eastern half of the US. Business days are Monday to Friday, and weekends and federal holidays do not count. Add the two together and count forward from the day your payment was confirmed, not the day you placed the order.

Here is a worked example. You pay on a Monday. Processing runs until Wednesday or Thursday. If you live in the east, transit adds 11 to 18 business days, so delivery could fall in the third to fifth week. If you live in Arizona, delivery could fall the week after shipping. A parcel that is five business days into an eleven-day estimate is not late, however long it feels. See [shipping times from Phoenix, Arizona](/blog/shipping-times-from-phoenix-arizona/) for a fuller picture.

## 2. Look at tracking
Open your tracking email or your private order page. Our page tells you whether payment is confirmed and whether the order has shipped. The carrier's tracking page tells you where the parcel is. Updates can pause for several days in regional carrier networks, so a tracking history that has not moved for two or three days is not unusual. Look for the last event: label created, accepted, in transit, out for delivery, delivery attempted or delivered. Each tells you something different. See [how to track your order](/blog/how-to-track-your-order/) for what each event means.

## 3. Look for a delivery notice
Because an adult must sign for every delivery, carriers often leave a notice after a missed attempt. Check your door, your mailbox, your building's package area and your phone for a call or a text. If you find a notice, follow its instructions straight away: many carriers let you schedule a redelivery, choose a time window or collect the parcel from a depot with ID. If the carrier makes several unsuccessful attempts it may return the parcel, which can add weeks, so act quickly.

## 4. Confirm your address
Make sure the address on your order is correct, including apartment, suite and unit numbers and the ZIP code. A small error can send a parcel astray or make it undeliverable. Your confirmation email and your private order page show the address you submitted. If it is wrong, contact us immediately. We cannot change the address after the parcel is handed to the carrier, but the sooner we know, the more we can try. See [shipping address tips](/blog/shipping-address-tips/).

## 5. Contact the carrier
If tracking shows delivered but you do not have the parcel, call the carrier with your tracking number. Ask where and when it was delivered, who signed and whether a photo or signature is on file. Because signature is required, a delivered status should have a signature record. Check with neighbors, building staff and others at the address, because someone may have signed on your behalf where the carrier allows it. If the carrier cannot account for the parcel, tell us what you learned.

## 6. Contact us
If the estimated window has passed, email, message or call us with your order ID. Business contact options are on the [contact page](/contact/), and customer service hours are Monday to Saturday, 9AM to 7PM Pacific Standard Time. Include your order ID, the tracking number, the carrier name, the date you expected delivery and what you have already checked. We will look at the order and the tracking, contact the carrier where that helps and tell you what we find. A short, complete message gets the quickest answer.

## What if the tracking never started?
A label that was created but never scanned means the carrier has not yet taken the parcel into its network. Sometimes that is a delay of a day or two. If it has been longer than that, tell us, and we will check with the carrier. It is not something you can fix at your end, but telling us promptly helps.

## Returned packages
If a carrier returns an undelivered package, for example because no one was available to sign, a refund is available minus the 15% restocking fee and the shipping cost, per the shipping policy. You will not lose the whole amount, but you will lose the fees, which is why it is worth planning for the signature. If you see a notice, arrange redelivery before the parcel is sent back. See [adult signature on delivery](/blog/adult-signature-on-delivery-what-to-expect/).

## Lost, stolen or damaged
Our shipping policy explains how these cases are handled, including package protection where it applies. If your parcel is lost or stolen, or you did not receive protection and want to discuss it, call or email us and we will explain what is possible. For damage, photograph the items and the invoice immediately and email our support team with the photos, as the policy says, and we will help you reorder damaged items. See [damaged or missing items](/blog/damaged-or-missing-items-what-to-do/).

## How to avoid delays next time
- **Order early.** Do not wait until you are almost out, especially in the east.
- **Pay promptly.** Processing starts when payment is confirmed.
- **Use an address where an adult will be.** A missed signature is the most common cause of delay.
- **Include every address detail.** Apartment numbers and ZIP codes matter.
- **Keep your phone on.** The carrier may call.
- **Watch for tracking updates** and any delivery notice.
- **Allow extra time around holidays.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### How long should I wait before contacting you?
If your order is inside the estimate for your region, give it time. If it is outside, contact us. If tracking shows an exception, such as a returned parcel, contact us straight away.

### Can you speed up a delayed parcel?
We cannot make a carrier move faster, but we can contact the carrier, check for problems and advise you. Sometimes a call from us is enough to find a stuck parcel.

### Can I get my money back if it is very late?
If a parcel is lost or returned, our policy describes the refund and replacement options. If it is simply slow, the estimates apply. Contact us and we will explain what applies to your order.

### Should I order again while I wait?
Please contact us first. Ordering again can lead to duplicate parcels, and we can usually tell you whether the first is likely to arrive.

### What if the address is in a remote area?
Delivery to remote areas can take longer, and some excluded territories are not covered by free shipping. Contact us if you are unsure. See [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

## A checklist before you contact us
1. Counted processing plus transit from the day payment was confirmed.
2. Checked the carrier's tracking page and our order page.
3. Looked for a delivery notice and any missed-delivery messages.
4. Confirmed the address on your order.
5. Spoken to anyone else at the address.
6. Collected your order ID and tracking number.

With those in hand, we can usually resolve the question in one reply. Browse [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/) and [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) when you are ready to order again. All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A short guide to talking to the carrier
Carriers deal with thousands of calls, and a prepared caller gets better results. Have your tracking number, the delivery address and the date you expected the parcel. Ask for the last scan location and time, whether a delivery was attempted, whether a signature was recorded and whether there is a hold or an exception on the parcel. Write down the name or reference number of the person you speak to. If the carrier says it will investigate, ask when you can expect an update, and share that with us so that we can follow up on our side too.

## Staying calm while you wait
Most delayed parcels do arrive. Long routes, regional networks and signature attempts explain the majority of delays, and a parcel that is slow is not the same as a parcel that is lost. If you are close to running out of a product, tell us, and we will talk through your options. Avoid placing a second order before we have checked, because you might end up with two parcels and a more complicated situation to sort out.

faq.q: How do I know if my package is actually late?
faq.a: Add our 24 to 72 business hours of processing to the carrier estimate for your region (3 to 7 business days West Coast, 11 to 18 eastern half), counting from payment confirmation and excluding weekends and holidays.

faq.q: What if tracking has not updated for days?
faq.a: Updates can pause for several days in regional carrier networks. Check the last event and compare with the estimate before worrying.

faq.q: What if it says delivered but I do not have it?
faq.a: Call the carrier with your tracking number, ask who signed, check with others at the address and then contact us.

faq.q: What happens if the carrier returns the parcel?
faq.a: A refund is available minus the 15% restocking fee and the shipping cost, per the shipping policy.
Check tracking and the address, then contact the carrier if it says delivered, and contact us with your order ID if the estimate has passed.
Photograph the items and invoice immediately and email us. We will help you reorder damaged items.
